pattern: data availability|availability of data|data accessibility|data and code are available
msg: No data availability statement. Springer Nature, Elsevier and PLOS all ask for one at submission, and the editorial office checks it before the paper reaches an editor.
No funding statement. Funders and publishers require the grant source (or an explicit 'no funding') in the manuscript itself, not only in the submission form.

pattern: competing interest|conflict of interest|declaration of interest|conflicts of interest
msg: No declaration of competing interest. ICMJE-following journals require the declaration inside the manuscript; a blank one is still a statement and must be written out.
No author contribution (CRediT) statement. Elsevier, Springer Nature and PLOS map each author to CRediT roles; missing roles bounce back as an author query.

pattern: generative ai|large language model|chatgpt|ai-assisted|ai tool|artificial intelligence was|no ai was
msg: No statement about generative-AI use. Publishers following the ICMJE recommendations ask authors to say whether an AI tool was used in writing, and to say so even when it was not.
No ORCID iD in the manuscript. Several journals make ORCID mandatory for the corresponding author and will hold the submission until it is supplied.
No abstract environment found. Submission systems parse the abstract out of the source; without it the record is created empty and the paper is returned.
No keywords. Keywords drive reviewer matching in the editorial system; a paper with none is slower to assign and easier to desk-reject.
Line numbers are not switched on. Journals that send the PDF straight to reviewers require continuous line numbering (lineno + \linenumbers) at first submission.
Obsolete package. Publisher build farms run current TeX Live and reject sources that load subfigure, epsfig, psfig, caption2, epsf, t1enc or here; use subcaption and graphicx instead.
The document class is still in draft mode, so figures compile as empty boxes and overfull rules are printed into the PDF the editor sees.
Absolute path to a figure. The publisher compiles the upload on their own machine, where this path does not exist, and the build fails without ever reaching an editor.
Figure is EPS/PS/BMP. pdflatex on the publisher side takes PDF, PNG or JPG; legacy formats either fail the build or are downsampled into the proof.
An editing note is still in the source. Draft notes printed in the margin or left in a comment are read by the editor and are the cheapest reason to be sent back.
The manuscript is split across files. Most submission systems want one flattened .tex plus the .bbl; every included file has to be checked too before you upload.
An acknowledgements section names your lab and funders. For a double-anonymous journal that identifies you, and the paper is returned unreviewed.
The manuscript is dated {year} but you are submitting on {today}. A prior-year date on the title page reads as a paper that was already rejected somewhere else.
